source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: In the live skill-editing discussion, how was "narrative" distinguished from "expository"?

options.text: Narrative means telling a story about something; expository means explaining it directly
options.feedback: This is exactly the distinction drawn: narrative tells a story about the class, while expository explains the material directly -- and the notes needed the latter to support detailed quiz questions.

options.text: Narrative means using screenshots; expository means using text only
options.feedback: The distinction was about a mode of explanation, not about the presence or absence of screenshots -- screenshots were discussed separately as an assignment option for personalizing the skill.

options.text: Narrative means writing in the first person; expository means writing in the second person
options.feedback: Person (first versus second) is a different stylistic axis than narrative versus expository, and it was not the contrast drawn in this discussion.

options.text: Narrative means a shorter document; expository means a longer one
options.feedback: Document length was not the distinction being made -- the concern was whether the writing explains concepts directly or tells a story about them, regardless of how long it runs.
